title: A Formal Audit of a Categorical Unification of Consciousness Theories: Structural Proxies, Formal Obstructions and a Positive Route

creators.name: Toranzo Portela, Ángel José
creators.affiliation: Independent Researcher in Theoretical Physics and Cognitive Science

description:
Version 1.2 (19 November 2026); the changes from versions 1.0 and 1.1 are listed in CHANGES.md. Version 1.0 has the DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24349944, and version 1.1 the DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24361411.

Several theories of consciousness, among them integrated information theory (IIT), global neuronal workspace theory (GNWT) and attention schema theory, together with general frameworks that have been brought to bear on consciousness, such as the free-energy principle (FEP) and quantum Darwinism, describe the same open physical systems through different invariants. A candidate theory, Q, formulated by the author and defined in this paper, proposes to unify them categorically. We audit this unification formally and structurally, to delimit with mathematical precision which parts of it can be established and which promises of unification fail, for explicit structural proxies of the theories, not for the theories themselves. The test case is the unity-sufficiency obligation S_u of Q; the audit does not change the descriptor, the domain or the meaning of Q. Results are labelled by their evidence: proofs checked by the Lean 4 kernel, paper proofs, exact computation, or numerics.

(I) Negative delimitation. The weak categorical thesis holds, but cheaply: every isomorphism-invariant assignment is a functor out of a symmetric monoidal groupoid of open systems. For the presence proxies of IIT type (a Gaussian integration functional J > 0, not the Φ of IIT 3.0) and GNWT type (a broadcast hub of the undirected coupling graph, a structural stand-in that models neither ignition nor dynamic broadcast) there is no translation between the projections, their bridge square does not commute, and neither is monoidal into the additive reals: both vanish on systems with disconnected support, in particular on tensor products of nonempty systems, and with the empty system sent to an adjoined unit they are strong monoidal into a zero-product monoid, whereas predictive information is additive. The two proxies disagree exactly on a band of connected systems without a hub, empty for n ≤ 3 units and containing the path P_n and the cycle C_n for every n ≥ 4. A premise “the degree depends only on κ” implies S_u exactly when the kernel of the descriptor lies in the equivalence it generates, and none of the principles examined closes S_u without presupposing it, equating only isomorphic realizations, forcing a constant degree, changing the meaning of the degree, or changing the domain. A conditional theorem extends this criterion to the sufficiency obligation of every component of Q, to its order clause and to its descent condition: it states which premises would discharge each of these obligations, and justifies none of them.

(II) A Gaussian laboratory, exact in a two-unit family and numerical in four-unit networks, illustrates where the bridges commute and where they break, and shows exactly that the min-cut lower bound on J is attained.

(III) Of the reformulations examined, only intervention monotonicity escapes the collapse; it is a declared weakening of the order clause of Q, not S_u, and we have not shown that it is the only one. Degrees of the form f∘κ that satisfy intervention monotonicity are forced to be constant exactly on the strongly connected components of an intervention digraph. With J as a stand-in for the descriptor of Q, on systems with at least two units, J increases strictly under uniform scaling of any connected dynamics, or with a fixed scalar self-coupling (checked in Lean with Mathlib, as are the equivalence of J > 0 with connected support and the min-cut bounds on J), but it can decrease against a fixed non-scalar self-coupling.

Q is neither demonstrated nor refuted. Seven Lean files without Mathlib and a Lean project with Mathlib of eight modules, all without sorry, and fifteen scripts archived with the paper reproduce every result labelled as checked by Lean, by exact computation or numerically.

This record contains:

  • the paper, as a PDF and as LaTeX source in the Compositionality template, with the unpublished option;
  • seven Lean 4 files, checked with Lean 4.24.0 without Mathlib: exit code 0, no sorry, and only the standard axioms;
  • a Lean 4 project with Mathlib v4.24.0 (eight modules) that checks three analytic results on J (the connectivity lemma, the min-cut sandwich and the scaling proposition) and the exact frontier of intervention monotonicity with real-valued degrees, with only the standard axioms;
  • fifteen Python scripts (exact SymPy computations, numerical illustrations and exact counts) with their expected outputs, among them the second check of the four-unit networks, which version 1.0 cited without archiving it;
  • three scripts that rerun everything and compare the results, and a master script, verify_all.sh (or make verify), that first checks the SHA-256 sums of all files and then runs them in turn (see README.md).
  • CHANGES.md, the list of changes from versions 1.0 and 1.1.

Use of generative AI: the paper was drafted, and its Lean files and scripts were written and run, by an AI assistant (Claude Code, by Anthropic, with Anthropic's Claude models), at the request and under the direction of the author, who is responsible for the content. Agents of the same assistant read primary sources, verified the Gaussian family, translated version 1.0 of the paper from its Spanish master version (the changes of version 1.1 were written in English), formalized the analytic results in Lean with Mathlib and reviewed the work adversarially; the pre-submission review that led to version 1.1 (its adversarial verification, the conditional theorem and its Lean file, the Lean module with real-valued degrees and the archived second check of the four-unit networks) was also done by agents of the same assistant; their agreement is not an independent validation, and there has been no independent human review. The corrections and improvements of version 1.2 come from an adversarial verification, by agents of the same assistant, of a reading of version 1.1 that the author made in conversations with Claude (Anthropic) outside Claude Code; that reading was treated as unverified input, and the assistant applied the corrections and improvements, with no independent human review. During the research the author also used Claude, outside Claude Code, in exploratory conversations; that material was treated as unverified input, and no result of the paper depends on it. No AI system other than Anthropic's Claude was used. Only the statements labelled [L] or [M] are checked by the Lean kernel, in their logical form, and only those labelled [S] by exact computation.
